transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. The sparking and blue flashes on the right-hand wall are likely caused by metal objects, food splatter, or damage to the waveguide cover inside the cavity. Please switch off and unplug the microwave before doing anything else. With the power disconnected, remove any metal items or foil, then check if there is burnt residue on the small flat panel on the side wall or under the glass tray.

Ok, it's unplugged. There's no metal or foil in there, just a plain plastic bowl of soup earlier. The flat cardboard-like panel on the right wall has a black burnt spot with greasy splatter on it. There was a slight burnt smell and a wisp of smoke from that spot once, which stopped when I turned it off.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The burnt spot on the waveguide cover suggests why it sparked and smoked, but this damage means the microwave must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. The cover is designed to protect internal parts from food splatter, so once it burns through, it can cause repeated arcing or even damage the magnetron. Please do not try to run the appliance to test if it works now, as this could make the fault worse. With the power still unplugged and the door open, you can gently wipe away any loose grease around that burnt area using a damp cloth, but leave the cover itself alone.
